title.narrative: Output 3.1. Increased capacity of Member States to formulate and implement national employment policies in response to the COVID-19 crisis

description.narrative:
Following the Declaration on ensuring sustainable labour market integration of young people, signed on 8 July 2021 at the second EU-Western Balkans Ministerial Meeting on Employment and Social Affairs, ministries and institutions that have held responsibility for employment and labour market governance across subsequent governments in Montenegro have operationalized the Youth Guarantee, an innovative activation scheme targeting young women and men less than 30 years of age and which includes measures spanning across multiple policy areas, such as education, employment, and social protection. In line with the guidance received through the EU’s Economic and Investment Plan, which foresees four stages of implementation of the Youth Guarantee over multiple years, institutions in Montenegro have reached some of the key milestones foreseen under the first stage, albeit with significant delay due to some political instability. These milestones include: the establishment of a tripartite and multi-ministerial governance structure for the implementation of the Youth Guarantee and the identification of the sub-categories of NEETs to be targeted through the Youth Guarantee (this may change by the end of the year and the reporting should be revisited). Institutions involved in the delivery of the Youth Guarantee have also initiated a multi-year process of levelling up their capacities to implement the Youth Guarantee in line with the principles enshrined in the EU Council Recommendation of 30 October 2020 on A Bridge to Jobs – Reinforcing the Youth Guarantee In partnership with the European Commission (EC) and the European Training Foundation (ETF), the ILO has set up the EU-ILO Technical Assistance Facility on the Youth Guarantee in the Western Balkans, a demand-driven facility for the provision of high-quality technical assistance to countries implementing the Youth Guarantee. Based on the requests submitted through the Youth Guarantee Coordinator, the ILO has provided support in conducting the statistical mapping of youth not in education, employment, or training (NEET), the review of the policy and legal framework to assess preparedness for the implementation of the Youth Guarantee, the functional assessment of the public employment services and their capacity development requirements in order to function as service delivery mechanism for the Youth Guarantee. Additionally, the ILO has designed and delivered targeted capacity development programmes for the different institutions participating in the operationalization of the Youth Guarantee, including the social partners.
In Montenegro, institutions in charge of preparing the ground for the youth guarantee have relied significantly on the ILO’s facilitation of peer-learning and triangular cooperation with other public employment services from the region and from the EU, via South-South and Triangular Cooperation
